- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to prior peak.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above immediate prior high.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.33) and prices are trending up, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to capture momentum.
- Model frequently underestimates true price at 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed (0.00–0.33); apply a +1.5% bias to forecast if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive abruptly, model lags; forecast should be adjusted upward by 0.5–1.5% per day for 3–5 days post-shift.
- Mean reversion is evident when model forecasts are >10% above recent 7-day average; reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment is positive but price is flat or declining, model overreacts; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% to avoid overcorrection.
